findings.message: `block()` uses `re.search` with a multiline `^`, so it treats the first `<!-- clutch:meta` / `# clutch:meta` found anywhere in the file as the file's block. The ticket places the block at the top of a Markdown file (after any frontmatter) and, in Python, after the docstring or at the top. `docs/annotations-index-plan.md` is under the configured `docs/` root and has a valid example block inside a fenced code sample at lines 35-43. `check` reports that file as `drifted` instead of `missing`. `refresh` rewrites the example's `kind`, `verified` and `hash` in the middle of the plan document and never inserts the file's real block. The same happens for a Python file with a line-start marker inside a string, and line 29 raises `Malformed` for any line-start marker in body text.
findings.paved_road: Look for the block only at the insertion position `_position` computes (offset 0, right after the closing frontmatter fence, or right after the Python docstring), e.g. with `re.match` anchored at that offset. Text elsewhere is body. Add a unit test where a fenced example block in the body stays untouched and the file is reported `missing`.

findings.message: For `ast.ImportFrom`, only `node.module` is resolved, so `from clutch import meta` (the dominant import form in `tests/`, more than 250 files) yields `clutch/__init__.py` instead of `clutch/meta.py`. Generated `relates` then misses the repo modules the file actually imports, and `owner` becomes `clutch/__init__.py`. Because a non-empty `relates`/`owner` is never rewritten, the wrong values stick.
findings.paved_road: For `ImportFrom`, also try `module + '.' + alias.name` for each imported name (mapping to `<path>.py` or `<path>/__init__.py`), keeping the package path only when no submodule matches. Cover `from clutch import foo` in `tests/unit/test_meta_refresh.py`.
